findings.checklist_item: Add a regression test that simulates the NativeOutput branch raising a grammar-compilation rejection and asserts _pai_structured logs a WARNING and retries once on the PROMPTED branch (returning the PROMPTED result with the classified cause attached).
evidence: Plan: 'when the NativeOutput branch raises and translate_schema_complexity_rejection recognises it, log loudly and retry ONCE on the existing PROMPTED branch'
AC5 covers only classification ('SIMULATED provider grammar-compilation rejection and asserts it is not reported as an outage'), not the retry-and-succeed transition
The retry-once branch is conditional logic (recognised-rejection -> fallback) whose only listed exercise is the live review-plan replication
findings.finding: The new fallback branch in _pai_structured (NativeOutput raises -> translate_schema_complexity_rejection recognises -> log WARNING -> retry ONCE on PROMPTED) is a new failure-path with conditional logic, but no unit/regression AC pins that branch directly; the classification test (AC5) only asserts the rejection is recognised, and the only end-to-end exercise of the retry is the live `rebar review-plan` run. A test that drives the NativeOutput branch raising a simulated grammar-compilation rejection and asserts the code retries once on PROMPTED and returns the PROMPTED result would keep the fallback wiring from silently regressing without a live call.
scenarios: A future edit to structured_run.py breaks the retry wiring (e.g. does not re-invoke the PROMPTED branch, or drops the classified cause) but the simulated classification test and complexity-gate test both still pass green, so the offline suite does not catch it; only a live Bedrock run would.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the union pole the same way as the optional pole: state the expected union count per reproducing contract, and specify whether a single-type Literal enum ({enum,type:'string'}) counts as a union — reconciling the detection rule (anyOf/oneOf or list-valued type) with the enum shape pydantic actually emits for these contracts.
evidence: Plan: '…plus each property carrying anyOf/oneOf or a list-valued type (union)' and 'Bound: 16 optional / 12 union' and RCA 'complexity caps (24 optional parameters, 16 union-typed)'

verify_models.py defines the reproducing contracts' closed-set fields as pydantic Literal[...] (PlanSeverityAttrs.ac_unverifiable = Literal['none','underspecified_oracle','broken_oracle','missing_oracle']; divergent_implementation = Literal[...]) — a single-type Literal serializes to {'enum':[...],'type':'string'}, i.e. NOT anyOf/oneOf and NOT a list-valued 'type'

The plan pins OPTIONAL counts to exact values (10/14/22/31/36) but states NO union count for any contract, so the '12 union' bound has no reproduction to pin it and the walker's union branch is untestable against the real schema
findings.finding: The union pole of the complexity bound is under-specified and its detection rule likely mis-scores the reproducing contracts' enum fields: the plan pins a '12 union' bound and cites Anthropic's '16 union-typed' cap but gives no per-contract union counts, and its union rule (anyOf/oneOf or list-valued type) does not match the pydantic Literal enums those contracts actually emit.
findings.location: Approach part 1 ('The count MUST recurse' / bound '16 optional / 12 union')
scenarios: The union counter scores the reproducing contracts near 0 (their closed-set fields are enum-typed, not anyOf/oneOf), so the '12 union' half of the bound never fires and its correctness is never exercised — a silent no-op that appears implemented
If a contract's downgrade were ever intended to hinge on the union count rather than the optional count, the mis-scoring would let a genuinely union-heavy schema slip past the bound
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the union bound if the optional bound alone downgrades the three measured contracts (state that explicitly), or extend the union-detection rule to include single-type 'enum' schemas and pin per-contract union counts as reproduction fixtures alongside the optional counts.

findings.finding: The part-1 complexity predicate as specified may count the wrong properties: the reproducing contracts' 22/31/36 optional parameters are NOT top-level properties of the output contract's model_json_schema() — the top-level VerificationOutput has a single property (`verifications`, a list). The optional fields live in the NESTED Verification/Binary/SeverityAttrs models, reachable only via $defs/$ref, and the nested Verification even carries a REQUIRED field (`index`). A predicate counting only the top-level `properties` dict would see 1 and never exceed any bound, making the gate vacuous against the exact contracts it must catch.
findings.location: Approach part 1 (src/rebar/llm/structured.py): native_schema_supported(model_cls) 'counts OPTIONAL properties ... in model_json_schema()'
findings.suggested_fix: State that the predicate flattens/expands $defs before counting (e.g. walk every object node's `properties` minus its `required`, plus `anyOf`/`oneOf` union-typed props), and that the two-pole AC fixture must exercise a NESTED-optional contract shaped like VerificationOutput, not a flat top-level one.

findings.finding: The complexity-counting protocol native_schema_supported(model_cls) is under-specified where it matters most: it says 'count OPTIONAL properties in model_cls.model_json_schema()' but never states the count must RECURSE into nested model / list-item / $defs schemas. The target contracts (VerificationOutput) have exactly ONE top-level property — `verifications: list[Verification]` — and all 22-36 optionals live nested inside Verification.severity_attributes and Verification.binary. A literal reading (count of the top-level `properties`) yields 1, never exceeds any bound, and silently leaves NativeOutput ON — reproducing the exact defect the plan is fixing.
findings.location: Approach part 1 ('Gate native selection on schema complexity') and AC line 'output_mode returns PromptedOutput for a contract whose optional-parameter count exceeds the measured bound'
findings.suggested_fix: State that the predicate walks the resolved JSON Schema — dereferencing $defs and descending through `items` and nested object `properties` — and counts an optional property as any property NOT in its enclosing object's `required` list; cite that VerificationOutput exposes the 22-36 optionals only under verifications[].severity_attributes and verifications[].binary.
